We’re moving into a world where trust - between individuals, and even between nation states - feels like it’s steadily dissolving.

And because of that, trust itself becomes the real value. Not just what you say, but what you consistently stand behind. In a way, that’s the truest form of proof of work.

That’s why being a merchant on Nostr, selling a product, whatever it may be, in exchange for #Bitcoin, matters more than it might seem at first glance. It’s not just a transaction, but the signal.

You’re choosing to operate in an environment where both the money and the relationship demand a higher level of integrity.

That kind of trust isn’t easy to build. And it shouldn’t be taken lightly or viewed short-term.

Something that’s been on my mind lately when thinking about multi-planetary life and #Bitcoin:
Light (and therefore any digital data) takes anywhere from 3 to 22 minutes to travel between Earth and Mars. That’s longer than Bitcoin’s ~10-minute block interval.
Because of this fundamental latency, a single, synchronized blockchain simply couldn’t stay coherent across planets—the network would constantly fracture into competing chains.
Has anyone explored this problem (and potential solutions) in depth?
